name: Furniture
tagline: Loose pieces — specified by dimension, clearance and construction
description: Loose furniture is where a beautifully planned room succeeds or fails at 1:1. Every entry here leads with the dimensions and circulation clearances that decide whether a piece actually fits, then the construction that decides how long it lasts.

materials.name: Sofa
materials.blurb: Seat depth, back height and frame decide the comfort
materials.description: A 550–600 mm seat depth suits most Indian users; deeper looks generous in a showroom and unsupportive at home. Insist on a kiln-dried hardwood or steel frame and high-resilience foam.

materials.name: Dining table
materials.blurb: 600 mm of table edge per person, 900 mm of clearance behind
materials.description: Size the table by covers, then check the room: you need 900 mm from the table edge to the nearest wall for a chair to pull out and a person to pass behind it.

materials.name: Dining chair
materials.blurb: 450 mm seat height and 280–300 mm under the table
materials.description: The gap between seat top and table underside should be 280–300 mm — any less and legs do not fit, any more and diners perch. Armless chairs tuck in; arm chairs need a wider table.

materials.name: Bed
materials.blurb: Queen or king, with storage decided at drawing stage
materials.description: Indian queen is 60×78 inches and king 72×78 — always confirm the mattress size before the bed is made. Hydraulic storage needs 700 mm clearance above to lift.

materials.name: Side table
materials.blurb: Level with the sofa arm, within reach of the seat
materials.description: Height should match the sofa arm within 50 mm so a glass can be set down without looking. Two small tables usually work better than one large one.

materials.name: Coffee table
materials.blurb: Two-thirds the sofa length, 400 mm away from it
materials.description: Roughly two-thirds of the sofa's length looks right, at 400–450 mm from the seat edge so legs still pass. Nesting or paired tables suit rooms that get rearranged.

materials.name: TV unit
materials.blurb: Screen centre at seated eye level, cables planned in
materials.description: Seated eye level is around 1000–1100 mm, so a wall-mounted screen's centre should land there. Leave a cable route and a socket behind the unit before the joinery is fixed.

materials.name: Study table
materials.blurb: 750 mm high with real legroom and a light that works
materials.description: 750 mm top height, at least 600 mm of clear depth and 700 mm of knee width. Add a socket at desk level — a study table without power is a table.

materials.name: Office chair
materials.blurb: Adjustable seat height, lumbar support and armrests
materials.description: The one piece of furniture whose ergonomics affect health. Seat height 400–520 mm adjustable, adjustable lumbar and armrests, and a five-star base — anything less is decoration.

materials.name: Bar furniture
materials.blurb: Counter and stools coordinated by height — 750, 900 or 1050 mm
materials.description: Three standard heights and each needs its own stool: 750 mm table with a 450 mm seat, 900 mm counter with a 600 mm seat, 1050 mm bar with a 750 mm seat.

materials.name: Outdoor furniture
materials.blurb: Weather-rated frames and fabrics for balconies and terraces
materials.description: Powder-coated aluminium, teak or synthetic rattan over aluminium — never mild steel, which will bleed rust down the terrace within a monsoon. Cushions need solution-dyed acrylic fabric.
